correctness.rationale: Exhaustive cases partition all complete multipartite graphs: a part of size at least three, else a doubleton, else only singletons. Least-common-value greedy plus empty-bundle tie preference produces three nonempty bundles and proves EF1 via the last-received-item inequality. If all parts have size at most two, maximizing the lower singleton value of a chosen doubleton dominates the other selected doubleton after removal of one item. Giving agents goods from distinct parts blocks each leftover good at each agent. All-nonempty strictness and zero-valued monotone cases were explicitly covered. An analytical four-agent K3,3 proof matches the known obstruction. Exact exhaustive and random verification runs returned the stated counts; these do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The unsettled three-agent graph-conflict existence regime motivates a full positive classification on a natural structured family. The theorem covers arbitrary part sizes, any number of parts and any common normalized monotone set function, with a linear-query construction; thus it is not a finite slice or textbook exercise. The already-known four-agent K3,3 obstruction shows that its agent frontier is sharp.
